subject: Adding more information into the tooltip

messages.author: 5eb2ff758c7a6657
messages.subject: Adding more information into the tooltip
parts:
Hi,

is there a way to add more information to the tooltips in ggvis using tooltip() ?

The way I've done this is to use generate my own function to fit into the tooltip function
tooltip_info <- function(x=NULL) {
    if(is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    key = x["keys"][[1]]
        paste(
            'mpg: '    ,mtcars$mpg[key],'<br>',
            'cyl: '    , mtcars$cyl[key],'<br>',
            'disp: '    , mtcars$disp[key],'<br>',
            'hp: '    ,mtcars$hp[key]
         )
}     

mtcars$keys <- seq(1, nrow(mtcars))     
    ggvis(mtcars,
        props(
            x= ~mpg,
            y=~qsec,
            fill=~as.factor(cyl),
            key := ~keys)) + layer_point()+
tooltip(tooltip_info)


somewhat similar to how Thomas achieved this in an earlier post https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/ggvis/tooltips/ggvis/cVWAwrUvl78/805Vhg7WFYMJ

However I thought of adding arguements into my tooltip_info function but tooltip did not accept this as it only allows functions with a single argument. Any brave soul?

messages.author: 1161df5ae7a276da
messages.subject: Re: Adding more information into the tooltip
parts:
Hi Wesley,

Please keep in mind that I am a newbie at this. Perhaps I am more brave than knowledgeable. 

I think that one way around this is to use some "R magic" on your tooltip_info() function. FWIW, it looks like you are already doing this.

As you point out, your tooltip_info() function takes a single argument - this being a list describing the data under the mark. I gather this is the way for ggvis to specify which point you are interested in.

However, your tooltip function can use variables from its environment, just as you do by referring to mtcars in your function. 

The topic of functions and environments can be hairy - every time I need to sort it out, I have to go back to one of Hadley's Advanced R chapters: http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Environments.html

Perhaps your extra "arguments" could be supplied to your function this way (just as you have already)?

Anyhow, I hope this helps.

Ian

    do.call(paste,

    paste(var,': ',input$data[rowid,which(colnames(input$data) == var)],'<br>',sep="")
})

}

Hi Wesley,

Let me try to decrypt...

What I meant to say is that arguments are not the only way for functions to access information - they can also access their environment.

My suggestion was to see if there would be a workaround where additional information you would like to supply to the function using an argument could be supplied by the environment, instead.

Hope this helps,
